chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who slanders the young girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not whipped unless she has reached puberty or is near to it.'

key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: slanders (specifically in the legal context of hadd al-qadhf)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for whipping a man who slanders a young girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the fixed hadd penalty of eighty lashes for slander (qadhf) is contingent upon the victim's maturity, as the legal capacity to incur this specific punishment is tied to reaching bulugh. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction in Shia fiqh between the hadd for adults and the discretionary (ta'ir) punishment for minors, reflecting the principle that the full legal consequences of qadhf apply only when the slandered party is legally accountable. This nuance is crucial for understanding how classical scholars like al-Kulayni categorized evidentiary requirements in the Book of Hadd.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah <sup>asws</sup> about the man who slanders the young girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be whipped except if she happens to have matured or near to it’.
